page: OVHcloud b2-120 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Haswell processor running at 2.0 GHz, with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The hardware configuration includes 120.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB per core, alongside 400 GB of local SSD storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10% and Geekbench single-core in the bottom 25%. However, the 32 dedicated physical cores compensate in parallel workloads, yielding average multi-core performance across Geekbench, Passmark, and stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations also perform in the average tier.

Given the dedicated core allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance offers stable resource density for parallelized workloads. It is suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. However, it is poorly suited for single-threaded applications or intensive LLM text generation due to its legacy CPU architecture and low single-core clock speed.
